text:
jamie: heads-up: noticed a weird oscillation after yesterday's scale-down tweak. pools go idle -> scale-down -> immediate spike -> frantic scale-up -> back to idle. saw it across three shards.
ryan: ugh. did you correlate with tenant billing spikes or a synthetic load?
jamie: correlated with a background batch job that spikes every hour for ~90s. autoscaler treats it as traffic and spins up full nodes. by the time requests finish, cooldown expired and we scale down.
priya: sounds like our hysteresis and grace windows are too tight for intermittent bursty loads. we should add workload-shaped dampening.
marta: we tried fixed cooldowns before; they were either too long (wasted cost) or too short (oscillation). proposal: introduce a credit-based headroom where tenants earn amortized "warm credits" when they sustain steady usage, and spend them during bursts so admission avoids churn.
ops-lee: explain credits concretely - is this per-tenant or per-pool? what's the unit?
priya: sketch: credits are per-tenant (or per-queue) measured in token-seconds. baseline: 1 credit ~= 1s of a prewarmed slot at standard model. credits accumulate when tenant uses steady QPS above a threshold for > T_accumulate. on admission, if tenant has credits, they get fastpath admission without triggering new node provisioning until credits deplete.
jamie: benefit: short bursts consume credits, avoiding scale actions. drawback: long sustained bursts still need provisioning — credits can't mask that. also complexity: we need accounting and fair-share across tenants.
ryan: how do credits interact with pool-level burst lanes and reserved capacity?
priya: integrate: reserved capacity covers tenants with committed SLAs. credits apply to best-effort lane. pool burst lanes still exist — credits are a cheaper micro-warm pattern to avoid operator-scale churn for sub-minute spikes.
marta: operator changes needed? ideally minimal. control-plane should surface admission decision with fields: `admit_path: {fastpath|provision}` and `credit_used` count. operator only executes provisioning decisions already requested.
ops-lee: good. avoids operator having to implement credit logic. but then control-plane must be stable and scalable. also we must version the admission API.
jamie: testing plan: fuzz synthetic traces with Poisson spikes (10s-5m) and deterministic hourly batch. measure scale actions per hour, 95p latency, and cost delta. target: reduce scale actions by >40% for bursty tenants while keeping P95 within SLA.
ryan: what about safety: attacker could game credits by steady small traffic to bank credits then spike. need throttles and decay.
priya: propose credit decay half-life (e.g., credits decay 50% per 12h inactivity) and max cap per tenant tied to tier. also require a minimal cost_per_credit to avoid free banking.
marta: ops implications: auditing and reconciliation endpoint, exporter metrics: credits_balance{tenant}, credits_spent_total, fastpath_admits_total. add alert when fastpath_admits/core-provision ratio > 5 for a pool.
ops-lee: rollout: feature-flag credits in control-plane only; operator compatibility unchanged. step 1: simulate in staging with dry-run mode (control-plane logs decision but operator ignores). step 2: canary tenants opt-in via label `credit-beta`. step 3: full roll.
qa-bot: testcases queued: 1) hourly batch 90s spike 200 tenants, 2) slow bank-and-burst attack, 3) sustained 30m spike. expected outcomes attached in docs.
deploy-bot: control-plane/crediting dry-run -> starting canary at 2026-03-20T02:00Z
ryan: any thoughts on telemetry cost? new metrics could be high-cardinality. limit to tenant tiers and sampled traces for top consumers.
priya: yes, emit per-tenant only for top-N (by spend) and aggregated histograms for the rest. keep full audit logs in cold storage for reconciliation.
jamie: one more thing: reconcile with existing preemptible credits/soft-reservations. we should map preemptible credits to offset fastpath cost rather than double-count. i'll draft a short RFC with diagrams.
marta: +1. include runbook and rollback criteria: e.g., if pool-scale-actions not reduced or P95 regresses by > 10% for latency-critical tenants, rollback.
ops-lee: i'll add the canary checklist and add alerts.
jamie: thanks. I'll post the RFC in eng-runtime and link to the QA cases. ping me if you want to coauthor.
